facts: Riders are assigned/invited and must apply to participate.
Pre-meeting non-participation can lead to additional assignment/replacement.
Program officials verify participants and investigate ability, riding style and past results.
Bicycle name and gear ratio are recorded.
Missing entrants can be filled according to formal replacement procedures.
Initial race allocation considers ability, riding style, regional balance and other factors.
Rider number allocation considers ability, riding style and competition results.
Health/fitness and bicycle inspections are formal gates.
Failure can stop all or part of participation.
Formal judging monitors interference and rule violations.
Finish/winner determination is an official judging act with photo-finish support.
For later meeting days, finish order and progression rules determine advancing riders.
Tie, abandonment and race-not-established states have special progression handling.
Bet-type winner definitions, payout and invalid-vote/refund rules are legally specified and separate from the outcome model.

programming_consequences_for_science: Race samples are selected populations: rider composition depends on official assignment/programming processes, not only rider latent strength.
Race stage and meeting day encode real path dependence because previous finishes determine later advancement.
Class/grade/stage comparisons can be confounded by selection and advancement mechanisms.
Substitution and scratch handling need predeclared timestamp/state contracts rather than post-result row deletion.
A model trained on one venue/date/class/stage mix must not be generalized to all keirin without population evidence.
judgement_consequences_for_science: Ordered top3 is a useful modeling object but reality contains tie, DQ, abandonment, cancellation and race-not-established states.
A retrospective parser may fail-close these states for a clean benchmark, but a Digital Twin should represent the states explicitly rather than imply they do not exist.
Interference rules depend on action, degree, effect and race phase; simple binary tactical labels should not be declared equivalent to official infringement states.
market_separation: Bet-type and settlement rules belong to MARKET/SETTLEMENT modeling.
PAYOUT and post-race settlement must not enter sporting outcome features.
Scratch/refund rules can affect market probability normalization/settlement engineering but do not justify changing the sporting S0 without a separate prespec.

historical_note.warning: 2005 All-Star point, replacement and cancellation rules are retained as historical evidence and are not generalized to current generic competition without current corroboration.
